timeline.place: West Bank, Jerusalem, Sinai Peninsula, and Gaza Strip

timeline.event: Israel and Egypt agreed upon the Camp David Accords, proposing a Self-Governing Authority for the Arab population in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
A peace treaty based on the Camp David Accords was signed between Israel and Egypt.
Saudi Arabia put forward a peace plan based on a two-state settlement with support from the Arab League.
Israel completed its withdrawal from the Egyptian Sinai Peninsula and launched an invasion of Lebanon to expel the PLO.
Defense Minister Yitzhak Rabin added deportations to Israel's Iron Fist policy of cracking down on Palestinian nationalism.
Two Gaza students at Birzeit University were shot by Israeli soldiers on campus, triggering mass demonstrations and harsh punitive crackdowns.
A policy of deportation was introduced by Israeli authorities to intimidate activists.
IDF Lieutenant Ron Tal was shot dead at point-blank range while stuck in a Gaza traffic jam.
The IDF ambushed and killed seven Gazan men affiliated with Islamic Jihad who had escaped from prison.
The Arab summit in Amman focused on the Iran–Iraq War, shunting the Palestinian issue to the sidelines.
Six Israeli soldiers were killed in a Palestinian guerrilla operation known as the Night of the Gliders.
An Israeli truck collided with cars at the Erez checkpoint, killing four Palestinian workers and injuring seven others.
Palestinian teenagers threw stones at military vehicles, and Israeli soldiers fired back, killing 17-year-old Hatem Al-Sesi and marking the start of the Intifada.
Rioters threw a gasoline bomb at the U.S. consulate in East Jerusalem.
Ahmed Yassin founded the Hamas movement following the outbreak of the First Intifada.
The Israeli army closed Hebron University as part of collective punishment measures.
The IDF crippled Palestinian Islamic Jihad by arresting many of its leaders and members.
PLO leader Khalil al-Wazir (Abu Jihad) was assassinated in Tunis by an Israeli commando squad, triggering major riots in Gaza and the West Bank.
The Arab League agreed to support the Intifada financially at its summit.
An Israeli soldier was stabbed in an armed attack by militant factions.
The UN General Assembly condemned Israel by a large majority for its actions against the Intifada.
The PLO proclaimed the independent State of Palestine.
Yasser Arafat gave speeches repudiating terrorism and accepting UN Resolution 242 and Israel's right to exist.
The United States vetoed a draft UN Security Council resolution deploring Israel's disregard of resolutions and the Fourth Geneva Convention.
Yasser Arafat was elected president of the proclaimed State of Palestine by the Central Council of the PNC.
The United States vetoed a second UN Security Council draft resolution condemning Israel.
The United States vetoed a third UN Security Council draft resolution condemning alleged Israeli human rights violations.
Israeli police killed 22 Palestinians during clashes at the Al-Aqsa mosque on the Temple Mount.
The Israeli army's closure of Hebron University ended after more than three years.
The Madrid Conference convened to address the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
Palestinian militants initiated suicide car bombings with the Mehola Junction bombing in the Jordan Valley.
The Oslo Accords were signed between Israel and the PLO, establishing the Palestinian National Authority.
Baruch Goldstein killed 29 Palestinians in the Cave of the Patriarchs massacre, prompting Hamas to initiate lethal suicide attacks.
Hamas's top bomb maker Yahya Ayyash was killed by the IDF, prompting retaliatory suicide bombings.

legacy.what: The Madrid Conference was convened, bringing the conflict to international peace negotiations.
The Oslo Accords were signed, leading to the establishment of the Palestinian National Authority.
Yasser Arafat, Yitzhak Rabin, and Shimon Peres were awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for the Oslo negotiations.
The Second Intifada erupted in September, lasting until 2005.
Hamas won a majority in the Palestinian Legislative Council elections.
Hamas seized control of the Gaza Strip during the Battle of Gaza, leading to full Israeli and Egyptian blockades.

plan.question: How did a grassroots uprising reshape Middle Eastern leadership and ignite modern conflict?

cast.name: Yasser Arafat
cast.role: Chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization

chapters.title: A Decades-Long Occupation Ignites
beats: Twenty years after military conquest, simmering tensions explode across occupied territories as civil defiance challenges armed security forces.
A spontaneous street uprising brings widespread commercial strikes, mass stone-throwing, and lethal crackdowns to international attention.
The upheaval shatters decades of static military rule, elevating new militant rivals and forcing traditional political leadership into high-stakes diplomacy.

chapters.title: Old Rivals and New Challengers
beats: Gaza and the West Bank remain under military control following the Six-Day War, leaving millions of Palestinians without statehood while Israeli authorities establish security administration.
Israeli Defense Minister Yitzhak Rabin enforces an iron-fist doctrine, insisting on firm crackdowns, deportations, and military deterrence to crush Palestinian national ambitions.
Exiled in Tunis, Chairman Yasser Arafat leads the Palestine Liberation Organization, trying to maintain international relevance while Arab states turn their focus toward the Iran–Iraq War.
Khalil al-Wazir operates alongside Arafat as the PLO's senior military strategist, coordinating guerrilla networks and seeking to direct the struggle from abroad.
In Gaza, the cleric Ahmed Yassin organizes an Islamic welfare network, waiting for the political moment to challenge both Israeli control and secular Palestinian leadership.
chapters.hook: A fatal traffic accident in Gaza suddenly sparks a fire none of them can control.

chapters.title: The Spark at the Checkpoint
beats: An Israeli truck collision at the Erez checkpoint kills four Palestinian laborers, triggering furious street protests inside the nearby Jabalia refugee camp.
Troops open fire during clashes with stone-throwing youths, killing seventeen-year-old Hatem Al-Sesi and igniting nationwide unrest across Gaza and the West Bank.
Seeing the popular explosion, Ahmed Yassin organizes local activists to officially establish the militant Hamas movement, competing for leadership of the uprising.
Yitzhak Rabin responds by deploying tens of thousands of troops, authorizing commanders to suppress the spreading demonstrations through force.

chapters.title: The Commando Strike in Tunis
beats: Israeli intelligence targets Khalil al-Wazir as the remote-control coordinator funneling external support to the grassroots rebellion across the occupied territories.
An Israeli commando raid infiltrates his private residence in Tunis, assassinating Khalil al-Wazir in his home to sever the connection between exiled PLO leadership and local commanders.
The assassination ignites unprecedented rioting across Gaza and Jerusalem, convincing Yasser Arafat that external leadership must seize the political initiative or lose control entirely.

chapters.title: The Battle for the Streets
beats: Israeli security forces implement Yitzhak Rabin's policy of might, power and beatings, razing over two thousand homes and deploying up to 80,000 soldiers to enforce military curfews.
Yasser Arafat moves diplomatically to harness the uprising, orchestrating a formal declaration of an independent State of Palestine at a conference in Algiers.
On the ground, internal violence escalates dramatically as suspected collaborators are purged, while Ahmed Yassin's Hamas rejects secular moderation and expands radical resistance.
Lethal clashes at the Al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem leave 22 Palestinians dead, drawing broad international condemnation and cementing deep diplomatic stalemate.

chapters.title: The Road to Oslo and Beyond
beats: The First Intifada transitions to the diplomatic table as the 1991 Madrid Conference gathers regional powers, eventually leading to direct secret talks.
In 1993, Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat sign the Oslo Accords, formally establishing the Palestinian National Authority and earning the 1994 Nobel Peace Prize.
Ahmed Yassin's Hamas violently rejects the peace accords, introducing coordinated suicide bombings that destabilize security across the region.
The collapse of long-term negotiations triggers the eruption of the Second Intifada in 2000, bringing five more years of armed conflict.
By 2006, Hamas wins a legislative majority, subsequently seizing total control of Gaza in 2007 to establish an enduring military standoff.
